A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MixGRPO. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original FLUX experiments on HPDv2, including preference scores, training overhead, ablations and qualitative comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds SD3.5-M LoRA comparisons in Table 3 and Figure 8.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 correct the stated execution order: advantages are calculated after sampling the entire group, rather than inside the image-generation loop. This is a limited pseudocode correction; the mixed sampling rules, GRPO loss, window schedules, Flash solver and hybrid inference remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both retain HPDv2 text-to-image preference alignment and its four prompt styles. The added SD3.5-M LoRA experiment changes model and training configuration, without introducing a different dataset, task or input domain.

E2.justification: v2 substantially broadens the evaluated competitors beyond FLUX and DanceGRPO. New Table 3 compares against base SD3.5-M, Flow-GRPO, offline Flow-DPO and online Flow-DPO; the original comparator sets remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds a distinct SD3.5-M LoRA evaluation using three rewards and MixGRPO sampling/optimization NFEs of 10/4, beyond the retained FLUX setup. Section 4.2 also replaces the integer-time description with normalized time t_i=i/T; this documentation revision does not establish that earlier experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 adds a portability check on SD3.5-M with LoRA, supported by Table 3 and Figure 8. Existing window scheduling, interval, size, stride, solver-order, sampling-budget and hybrid-inference analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training seed counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. Existing group-normalization statistics and t-SNE feature variances are unchanged; the new results use the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: All earlier tabulated values and qualitative samples are retained. Table 3 and Figure 8 add substantial evidence under the new SD3.5-M LoRA setting: MixGRPO reports HPS 0.3416, Pick Score 0.2360 and ImageReward 1.4854. Online DPO has higher ImageReward, 1.5001. These are newly reported comparisons, not improvements over v1 under identical settings.

T1.justification: New Appendix A supplies an explicit mixed-sampling distribution-equivalence proof, and Section 3.1 revises the formal reward definition to terminal-only rewards. However, the added proof is inconsistent as printed: expanding Eq. (13) gives a 3/2 coefficient on the diffusion Laplacian term, whereas Eq. (14) uses 1/2.

C1.justification: The main contributions and approximately 50%/71% training-time reduction claims remain. The introduction additionally attributes inefficiency to inconsistent gradients and claims that progressively moving the SDE window narrows exploration to achieve global optimization.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly connects early denoising changes to preference-model priorities and interprets the new experiments as demonstrating LoRA suitability. Its broad statement of superiority over Flow-DPO needs qualification: Table 3 gives online DPO a higher ImageReward than MixGRPO.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 explicitly documents normalized sampling time, while Appendices C–D clarify continuous versus discrete indices and the sampling/optimization phases. The existing optimizer, hardware and training-budget disclosures, and code/model access link, remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for LoRA, Flow-DPO and stochastic differential equations, and removes the Miao et al. diversity reference. It extends comparison positioning to Flow-DPO and Flow-GRPO, while largely retaining the related-work discussion.

P1.justification: Localized introduction and method rewrites clarify terminology and time indexing. v2 adds an algorithm-explanation appendix and acknowledgements, and reorganizes the appendices; most prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 3 and Figure 8, places Tables 2–3 side by side, and moves Algorithm 1 and the former main-text Figure 4 into appendices. Figure 2 receives revised time labels and denoising arrows. Existing plots and generated-image samples are retained.

improvement.justification: The SD3.5-M LoRA comparisons and clearer procedural documentation improve empirical breadth and readability. However, the newly added equivalence proof contains an invalid algebraic reduction in Eq. (14), and the Flow-DPO superiority statement needs qualification given online DPO's higher ImageReward. These substantive benefits and new correctness and interpretation problems prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
